Whenever someone yells "not all X are like that", you have to keep in mind that groups are defined in different ways. Sometimes the definition of the group is too open and generalizations about the group are unfounded. However, some groups are defined with enough constraints that general characteristics can be assigned.

When it comes to men, the skittles analogy fails because there are too few constraints on the group "men". To be a man, you simply must have the male sex. A Y chromosome, that is all. This characteristic of men tells you nothing about an individual man's propensity to rape.

When it comes to Islam, the skittles analogy works on some level because there are many constraints on the group "muslim". A muslim accepts the Quran as holy truth. A muslim holds Mohammed as a ivine prophet. A muslim believes in one god that will smite and ruthlessly punish sinners and infidels. The list goes on. Therefore, being a part of the group "muslim" tells you a lot about what a muslim believes and how they may act. How do you expect a muslim to behave towards homosexuals? Well, let's look in the Quran which by definition all muslims consider a divinely truthful text. How do you expect a muslim to view violent conquest and child marriage? Well, let's look to Mohammed which by definition all muslims consider a divine prophet.

When it comes to "generalizing", you can't dismiss the practice wholesale. It depends on the definition of the group being characterized.
